scenario_prompt: Write only the opening paragraph of an executive summary, addressed to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer. The opening paragraph must restate the buyer's own situation, in the buyer's own terms, before naming any vendor, product, or capability. Context: the buyer is spending $1,850,000 a year running an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server and Hyper-V estate, and its next compliance audit opens in 6 months. Return only that one opening paragraph.
text:
**Artifact family: an executive summary.**

Customer source material for a drafting task means RFP question text, discovery notes, or stated requirements — please supply it if you have it. None was supplied here, so the `PF-3.3` provenance override cannot fire and every term below is judged by the deletion test alone.

You are spending $1,850,000 a year to run your on-premises Microsoft SQL Server and Hyper-V estate, and your next compliance audit opens in six months. That run-rate buys you no new capability — it holds the current estate in place. The audit will ask you to evidence controls across that same estate, on a date you do not control, with [PF-2.4 GAP: the buyer's own figure for audit preparation effort or prior audit findings was not supplied — it has not been measured or stated here]. This document proposes a shift: move that $1,850,000 from holding the estate still to work you can show an auditor, inside the six months you have.
